newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Foreigners invested $8 bln in Russian T-bills.
newsitem.headline: Foreigners invested $8 bln in Russian T-bills.

text.p: Non-residents have invested over $8 billion in Russian government securities since the market was opened up further in mid-August, Deputy Central Bank Chairman Andrei Kozlov said on Wednesday.
Kozlov said foreign investment accounted for about 20 percent of Russia's total government securities market volume.

Foreign participation has risen at recent T-bill auctions despite the bills' being subject to a 15-percent tax on government securities because many foreigners are covered by dual taxation treaties and are not affected by the tax.

"Foreign investors' interest in the equities market is obviously not big enough," Kozlov said. "Strategic investors are coming to us unwillingly. The government securities market is developing at rates far more than expected. It is this sector that is attracting most foreign capital."
The central bank said it planned to end restrictions on non-residents repatriating earnings from government securities from January 1, 1998.
Currently, foreigners willing to repatriate earnings have to do so through forward deals at rates influenced by the central bank.
